overview: F3101 connects the signals to the maneuver sequence. Students should be able to brief how Lead passes a signal, how Wing acknowledges it, and how each basic formation maneuver is entered, flown, corrected, and discontinued if spacing becomes unsafe.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion Items

items.text: Visual signals only work when Lead is predictable, Wing is in position, and both aircraft understand exactly when the signal is acknowledged and executed.

children.text: Lead first verbalizes the signal over ICS during training, confirms Wing is in position, clears the area, then passes the signal high and visible above the canopy rail.
Most signals are passed for about 3 seconds; the cruise signal uses a longer cadence.
Lead stops the signal, looks to Wing, confirms the head-nod acknowledgment, then executes smoothly.
If Wing gives a no-head-shake or there is confusion, Lead repeats the signal or clarifies by radio.
Run-up directs both aircraft to set the briefed run-up power and check safety-of-flight items.
Kiss-off releases Wing to separate for takeoff, breakup, detach, or landing as briefed.
Cruise directs Wing to move from parade to cruise; Wing acknowledges, slides to the 60-degree bearing line, sets the directed power, and calls ready.
Crossunder directs Wing to cross behind and below Lead after stabilizing aft with proper step-down.
Breakup and rendezvous starts the break sequence only after Wing acknowledges and Lead gives the kiss-off.
Lead change uses a distinct signal: Lead taps the helmet on the side away from Wing, then deliberately points to Wing.
The new Lead acknowledges, looks forward, and flies a stable platform.
The new Wing keeps eyes on the new Lead and preserves separation during the transition.

items.text: The formation maneuver set is a progression: establish spacing on departure, stabilize in parade, correct errors early, then use planned geometry for turns, crossunders, breakup and rendezvous, and underruns.

children.text: Line up with runway-side discipline and complete the Lineup Checklist before takeoff.
For interval takeoff, Wing delays 5 seconds after Lead begins the takeoff roll, then rejoins using controlled closure.
During running rendezvous, Wing keeps Lead slightly above the horizon, arrives on bearing line, and limits closure to a safe, briefed value.
Parade is built on the 45-degree bearing line, wingtip clearance, and step-down.
Wing corrects in A-B-C order: altitude, bearing, closure/separation.
In turns, Wing anticipates radius-of-turn effects: reduce power when Lead turns into Wing and add power when Lead turns away.
For a crossunder, Wing first moves aft and slightly down, verifies nose-to-tail clearance, then crosses behind Lead at a walking pace.
Wing never passes directly under Lead.
After crossing, reestablish bearing, separation, and step-down before moving back into normal parade.
For breakup and rendezvous, Lead starts from 200 KIAS, level flight, Wing in position, and clear airspace.
Wing breaks at Lead's 3/9 line, keeps Lead in sight, stabilizes in trail, then rejoins with Lead on the horizon.
If closure, aspect, or step-down becomes unsafe, underrun early instead of pressing a bad rendezvous.

studyNotes.summary: F3101 should be studied as a signal-to-maneuver event: know the visual signal cadence, then brief the formation maneuver flow that follows each signal.

summary: F3101 ties visual-signal discipline to basic formation maneuver execution in the OFT.
title: Visual Signals and Formation Maneuvers
